source.title: Initialization of ReLUs for Dynamical Isometry

record.file_problem: The supplied text appears to be the complete paper; no garbling or cutoff is apparent.
record.tranche_reason: The paper compares initialization schemes in ReLU networks and reports classification accuracy after a fixed training budget, bearing on initialization and trainability but not directly measuring training error or learning speed.
record.gate_note: The paper also discusses cited prior work on initialization and trainability; those cited results are not recorded as rows. Figures 3–4 report test accuracy after 10^4 SGD steps, not training classification error.
record.test_reason: The study gives a specific theoretical qualification to V4: preserving expected squared signal norms with He initialization does not prevent finite-width signal distortion or increasing alignment of different inputs, which the authors argue impairs deep ReLU trainability. Its empirical rows measure test accuracy after a fixed budget, rather than training speed or successful optimization, and do not directly establish V4.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is broadly accurate as an account of the authors' conclusion. They derive exact finite-width signal distributions, argue that variance preservation alone leaves important trainability problems, and propose initial parameter sharing, with perfect dynamical isometry for the effective pre-activation map in the orthogonal variant. They interpret improved fixed-budget test accuracy as evidence of better trainability; they do not directly measure training speed or training-error convergence.
record.recipe_differences: Compares He initialization with Gaussian submatrix and orthogonal submatrix parameter-sharing schemes; fully connected ReLU classifiers, SGD, no batch normalization or data augmentation.
record.method_sensitivity: The reported accuracy depends on initialization, network depth and width; CIFAR-10 accuracy is lower than for convolutional architectures, and images were clipped to 28 × 28.

fits_no_version.finding: GSM and orthogonal-submatrix initialization give higher test accuracy after 10,000 SGD steps than He initialization; the authors describe greater reliability at larger widths and depths.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Initial parameter sharing improves fixed-budget generalization accuracy in fully connected ReLU classifiers on MNIST and cropped CIFAR-10.

record.peer_reviewed: Neural Information Processing Systems (33rd Conference on Neural Information Processing Systems, 2019)
record.problems: The experiments report classification test accuracy rather than training error or learning speed. Accuracy results are given as plots without exact numeric values in the text; the CIFAR-10 experiments use clipped images and fully connected networks.
record.rows_left_out: Figures 3–4 vary depth L=1 through 10. To stay within 60 rows, extracted L=1, 5, and 10 for each dataset, width, and initialization; omitted L=2–4 and L=6–9.

untested.parts: Training classification error in sufficiently large convolutional networks, including random or corrupted labels, and all stated recipe qualifications.
Teacher-student spurious minima and the effect of one or two extra student neurons.
Training-error degradation in plain batch-normalized convolutional networks, residual-shortcut controls, very deep tanh training, and Fixup.

Direct learning-speed and training-loss comparisons; maximum successfully trainable depth; very deep tanh orthogonal-versus-Gaussian comparisons; and 10,000-layer convolutional training. Fixed-budget test accuracy does not isolate these outcomes.
Above-threshold learning rates, loss recovery, curvature dynamics, edge-of-stability behavior, and divergence.
Controlled normalization comparisons, accuracy gain over training time, higher-learning-rate tolerance, and Fixup.

missing.what: The study's theoretical qualification of variance-preserving initialization: expected squared norms remain constant under He initialization, but the finite-width distribution changes and different inputs become increasingly aligned with depth; the authors explicitly connect this to impaired trainability.
missing.locator: Section 2.3, Corollary 3, Proposition 4, Theorem 5, Figures 1–2; Section 5

missing.what: The proposed remedy's theoretical properties: paired positive/negative weights transmit the full signed signal; GSM preserves expected variance and cosine distance, while orthogonal submatrices provide perfect dynamical isometry for the effective pre-activation map at initialization. These are theoretical properties, not measured learning-speed improvements.

record.verdict_notes: This study is not an original source for any listed version. Remove the record's empirical supports label and width-based limits_scope label: width-dependent test accuracy does not establish a qualification to V4. Learning rates are divided by depth, so cross-depth endpoint comparisons also change the learning-rate schedule. Intermediate depths are already declared in rows_left_out and are not additional missing results.

versions.untested_parts: Training classification error, CIFAR-100, random or corrupted labels, model size thresholds, and effects of early stopping or regularization are not tested.
No two-layer teacher-student problem or neuron-count sweep for spurious minima.
No comparison of plain and shortcut networks; the study does not test batch normalization or Fixup. Its networks use ReLU activations, not very deep tanh networks.

No direct learning-speed measurement, gradient/signal propagation measurement during training, orthogonal Gaussian comparison at matched variance, or convolutional networks. The reported experiments are fully connected ReLU networks on MNIST and CIFAR-10.
No learning-rate stability or catapult-phase experiment.
